title: Texas Saltwater Limits
generalRules: You need a Texas fishing license with a saltwater endorsement.
These limits cover Texas waters out to 9 nautical miles, plus fish caught farther out and landed in Texas. Federal rules also apply past 9 nautical miles for some species.
Possession limit is twice the daily bag unless a fish's page says otherwise.
Fish that TPWD doesn't list have no state bag, possession, or size limits.
TPWD can change rules mid-season, like closures after a hard freeze. Check their site before you go.
measuring: Lay the fish on its side with its mouth closed.
Soft tail: squeeze the tail fin together. Hard tail: turn the tail to stretch it to its longest.
Measure in a straight line from the tip of the snout to the farthest tip of the tail.

fish.name: Redfish

overMax.note: Over the slot. Keep it only with your Red Drum Tag or Bonus Red Drum Tag. Otherwise, release it.

rules: Slot fish: 20 to 28 inches.
Per license year, you can keep one red over 28 inches with a Red Drum Tag, plus one more with a Bonus Red Drum Tag. Tagged fish don't count toward your daily bag.
Digital tags are reported in the Texas Hunt & Fish app instead of attached.
idTips: One or more black spots near the tail
Bronze to copper color
Mouth points down for feeding on the bottom
fish.where: Shallow flats, marsh edges, and oyster reefs. Big bull reds run the surf and passes in the fall.

fish.name: Speckled Trout

overMax.note: Over 28 inches. Keep it only with your Spotted Seatrout Tag or Bonus Spotted Seatrout Tag. Otherwise, release it.

rules: Keep fish from 15 to 20 inches. Fish from 20 to 28 inches go back.
Per license year, you can keep one trout over 28 inches with a Spotted Seatrout Tag, plus one more with a Bonus Spotted Seatrout Tag. Tagged fish don't count toward your daily bag.
idTips: Black spots on the back, back fin, and tail
Silver-gray with a darker back
Two big fangs at the tip of the upper jaw
fish.where: Grass flats, guts, and shell in the bay. Deeper channels when it's cold.

fish.name: Flounder

closures.note: Flounder season is closed Nov 1 through Dec 14 (bag limit 0).

rules: Closed every year from Nov 1 through Dec 14. Release every flounder during that time.
The rest of the year: 5 per day, 15 inch minimum.
Possession limit equals the daily bag (5), not double.
idTips: Flat, with both eyes on the top side
Brown with blurry dark and light blotches, not three sharp eyespots like a Gulf flounder
Big mouth with sharp teeth
fish.where: Sandy or muddy bottom near drop-offs, marsh drains, and pilings. They lie still and ambush bait.

fish.name: Black Drum

overMax.note: Over 52 inches. You may keep one this size per day, and it counts toward your daily bag.

rules: Keep fish from 14 to 30 inches.
You may also keep one black drum over 52 inches per day. It counts toward your bag and possession limits.
idTips: Tall, arched back
Rows of short whiskers under the chin
Young ones have 4 or 5 dark vertical bars. No tail spot.
fish.where: Channels, piers, jetties, and oyster reefs. Shrimp, crab, and cut bait on the bottom.

fish.name: Sheepshead
rules: 15 inch minimum, no maximum.
idTips: 5 to 7 bold black vertical bars
Teeth that look like human teeth
Sharp spines on the back fin
fish.where: Pilings, jetties, docks, and oyster reefs. Small hooks with shrimp or fiddler crab.

fish.name: Sand Trout
rules: Not on TPWD's limit list, so there's no state bag or size limit.
idTips: Pale tan to silver with no spots
Shaped like a speckled trout
Yellowish back and fins
fish.where: Deeper bay channels and passes, often in schools in winter.

fish.name: Atlantic Croaker
rules: Not on TPWD's limit list, so there's no state bag or size limit.
idTips: Silver-bronze with wavy brassy streaks on the back
Small whiskers on the chin
Makes a croaking sound when caught
fish.where: Muddy bay bottoms, channels, and piers. Also a popular live bait for trout.

fish.name: Gafftopsail Catfish
rules: No bag limit, but the minimum length is 14 inches.
Fin spines can cause painful wounds. Handle carefully.
idTips: Long fleshy streamers on the back and side fins
Two long, flat whiskers at the mouth
Very slimy coat
fish.where: Bays and surf in warm months. Hits shrimp and cut bait.

fish.name: Hardhead Catfish
rules: Not on TPWD's limit list, so there's no state bag or size limit.
Fin spines can cause painful wounds. Handle carefully.
idTips: Several short whiskers, no long fin streamers
Gray back, white belly
Hard bony plate on top of the head
fish.where: Nearly everywhere in the bay, usually stealing your bait.

fish.name: Striped Mullet

seasonal.note: October through January, mullet over 12 inches can't be kept or held on a boat.

rules: No bag or size limits February through September.
October through January, you can't keep mullet over 12 inches.
idTips: Torpedo shape with a blunt head
Dark stripes running along the sides
Two small, widely spaced back fins
fish.where: Schools on flats and in the marsh. Usually caught with a cast net for bait.

fish.name: Snook
rules: Slot fish: 24 to 28 inches, 1 per day.
idTips: Bold black line down the side
Lower jaw sticks out past the upper
Sloping forehead and yellowish fins
fish.where: Mostly the lower coast. Rare around Galveston.

fish.name: Whiting
rules: Not on TPWD's limit list, so there's no state bag or size limit.
idTips: One short whisker on the chin
Slim and silvery-gray with faint dusky bars
Small mouth set under the snout
fish.where: Surf troughs along the beach and bay passes. Shrimp or sand fleas on the bottom.

fish.name: Spanish Mackerel
rules: 14 inch minimum, 15 per day.
idTips: Gold or yellow oval spots on the sides
Long, slim, silver body with a forked tail
Sharp teeth
fish.where: Jetties and surf in warm months, chasing bait. Small spoons and jigs with a fast retrieve.

fish.name: Florida Pompano
rules: Not on TPWD's limit list, so there's no state bag or size limit.
idTips: Deep, flat, silver body
Yellow belly and fins
Blunt head and deeply forked tail
fish.where: Surf troughs, especially in spring and fall. Sand fleas or shrimp on the bottom.

fish.name: Jack Crevalle
rules: Not on TPWD's limit list, so there's no state bag or size limit.
idTips: Steep, blunt forehead
Black spot on the gill cover and on the side fin
Hard ridge of scales near the tail
fish.where: Jetties, passes, and surf in summer. Hard fighters, often in big schools.

fish.name: Bluefish
rules: Not on TPWD's limit list, so there's no state bag or size limit.
idTips: Blue-green back and silver sides
Big mouth full of sharp teeth
Dark blotch at the base of the side fin
fish.where: Surf and jetties. Watch your fingers.

fish.name: Blacktip Shark
rules: 1 shark per person per day, all kinds combined.
Blacktip, Atlantic sharpnose, and bonnethead: 24 inch minimum. Most other legal sharks: 64 inches. Hammerheads: 99 inches.
You must use non-offset, non-stainless steel circle hooks when fishing for sharks.
Many sharks are catch-and-release only, including sandbar, dusky, sand tiger, and silky. If you can't tell what it is, release it.
idTips: Black tips on the side fins and lower tail
Pointed snout
Faint white band along the side
fish.where: Surf and passes in summer. Fish-finder rig with cut bait.

fish.name: Bull Shark
rules: Falls under other allowed sharks: 64 inch minimum.
Counts toward the 1 shark per person per day limit.
You must use non-offset, non-stainless steel circle hooks when fishing for sharks.
idTips: Stocky gray body
Short, wide, blunt snout
Adults have no black fin tips
fish.where: Bays, passes, and surf in warm water. Dangerous to handle.

fish.name: Tarpon
rules: 85 inch minimum, so nearly every tarpon gets released.
idTips: Huge, shiny silver scales
Upturned mouth
Long thread trailing from the back fin
fish.where: Passes, jetties, and nearshore water in summer.

fish.name: King Mackerel
rules: 27 inch minimum, 3 per day.
idTips: Long, slim, gray-silver. Adults have no spots.
Side line dips sharply under the second back fin
Sharp teeth
fish.where: Nearshore rigs and reefs in warm months.

fish.name: Cobia
rules: 40 inch minimum, 1 per day.
idTips: Long dark-brown body with a dark stripe along the side
Broad, flat head
Row of short separate spines instead of a tall front back fin
fish.where: Near buoys, rigs, and floating debris, often following rays or sharks.

fish.name: Red Snapper
fish.checkNote: Based on Texas state-water rules. In federal waters, the minimum is 16 inches.
rules: Texas state waters (out to 9 nautical miles): open year-round, 4 per day, 15 inch minimum.
Federal waters: 2 per day, 16 inch minimum, and a season that changes each year. The 2026 federal season opened May 22. Check TPWD before you go.
Use a circle hook with natural bait, and a venting tool or descending device on fish with barotrauma.
idTips: Red-pink all over with a red eye
Pointed snout
Pointed anal fin
fish.where: Offshore reefs, rigs, and wrecks.

fish.name: Tripletail
rules: 17 inch minimum, 3 per day.
idTips: Rounded back and belly fins that look like three tails
Mottled brown to yellow
Floats on its side near structure
fish.where: Near buoys, channel markers, and floating weeds. Sometimes in the bay.

fish.name: Greater Amberjack
rules: 38 inch minimum, 1 per day.
The 2026 federal-water season ran Sept 1 to Oct 14. Check before fishing past 9 nautical miles.
Use a venting tool or descending device on fish with barotrauma.
idTips: Dark diagonal band from the snout through the eye
Amber stripe along the side
Olive-brown back and forked tail
fish.where: Offshore rigs and reefs.
